[b]March 14, 2025  The Palace of Etherniasti, Capital City
[/b]
A quiet tension filled the grand chamber of the Etherniasti government headquarters. The polished oak conference table was lined with military officials, intelligence officers, and advisors, their faces grave as they awaited the debriefing. At the head of the room sat Leader Reginold III, his fingers interlocked as he studied the encrypted documents before him.

The doors opened abruptly. Commander Jorin Tarris of the EHS Sea Hawk stepped forward, saluting sharply before placing a sealed dossier onto the table.

Sir, weve intercepted a critical transmission from Sal-Baliz military command. Theyre on high alertthey detected an unidentified helicopter near Jinarat and are mobilizing forces for an investigation.

A hushed murmur passed through the room. Foreign Minister Alaric Trevayne leaned forward, his expression dark.

This means an operation is already underway inside Sal-Baliz territory and its not one of ours.

General Othran Vale exhaled sharply. If this is Hydronias doing, they may have sent operatives without diplomatic clearance. If Sal-Baliz finds them, the situation could escalate beyond control.

Leader Reginold tapped his fingers against the table. We need confirmation. Have the EHS Sea Hawk maintain passive monitoring. No transmissions. If the situation escalates, we cannot be caught unprepared.

Intelligence Director Elira Myron spoke up. I recommend reaching out to Hydronia discreetly. If they confirm an ongoing operation, we may need to act preemptively to prevent an international crisis.

Reginolds face hardened. His nation was small, but he would not allow Etherniasti to be blindsided.

Effective immediately, place the navy and air force on 'Be Ready' status. I want all naval patrols heightened along our waters, and reconnaissance flights prepared for immediate deployment if necessary. We do not act unless provokedbut we must be ready for anything.

The assembled officials nodded, understanding the weight of his command. Across Etherniasti, the wheels of its modest but disciplined military began turning. At naval bases, crews rushed to their stations. Airstrips that had been quiet moments before now buzzed with the hum of engines preparing for takeoff. Fighter jets were placed on standby, and ships readied for rapid deployment.

As the meeting adjourned, an air of unease lingered over the capital. Across the seas, the EHS Sea Hawk floated in silence, listening to the currents of war shift ever closer to Etherniastis shores.

Etherniasti was watching. And waiting.

[b]A Traitor's Death[/b]
[sub][/sub]]
[i]Abdul Al-Sybu sat in on the meeting. There was some terrorist organisation to the north, nothing to be alarmed about really, some alliance was already planning to crush it but there was a meeting nonetheless. You never know, we must always stay vigilant Said Grand Air Marshal Ahmed 'the Hawk' al-Nazim. Abdul didnt really care; he had long since been tuned out to the discussion. 

He had even begun to nod off before he heard the opening of the iron door into their meeting room. He had at first thought the meeting was over until he opened his eyes and saw them. Agents of the Order of Silence named as such because they silence those who are against the Sealiphate. Abduls eyes widened slightly, while all in the Order dressed eccentrically to say the least, he recognized one of the uniforms, Hasan the Unmaker, his longsword hanging from his side. 

Ahmed 'the Hawk' sheepishly raised his voice. Why are you here, sir? Hasan did not respond as he pointed his steel gauntlet-covered hand at Abdul al-Sybu gesturing him to follow. As Abdul looked upon the giant armour-clad man he felt fear, did they perhaps know his secret? He followed regardless, better to follow and have a chance of escape then not and be killed on the spot.

His eyes drifted down towards the longsword as he walked behind Hasan. Abdulk tried to make small talk but the Order of Silence agents were surprisingly silent. They walked out of the bunker into the daylight, the scorching sun of Irocco beating down on Abdul dressed in all that military cloth. He looked once more upon the armour of Hasan. You must be sweating under that huh? Abdul said, trying to joke around with the man. ... Hasan said in reply.

He pointed toward a car before entering it himself, followed by the other agent. This was enough of a sign for Abdul to likewise enter. He sat in the back. They drove for a time before stopping, the agent in the passenger seat stepped out of the car and opened the door for Abdul. When Abdul got out, the agent injected something into his neck and he fell unconscious into the hands of the agent who promptly stuffed him back in the car before re-entering himself.

Abdul's eyes opened; he did not know where he was or how long it had been. He reasoned he was in another bunker based on the concrete box he seemed to be in. Looking down, he realised he was strapped to some kind of chair. He looked toward the corner and there was Hasan lounging back in a chair that looked much more comfortable (and less bloodstained) than his. Abdul began to speak but was shushed partway into his sentence by the opening of the door.

Ahsan 'the One who Inquires' stepped through his robe touching the ground, his staff scraping the ceiling alongside his signature triangular helmet. He closed the door behind him with the back of his staff.

He seemed to be looking straight at Abdul but it was hard to tell with the helmet. From within the helmet words rang out with a slight echo. You must be Abdul al-Sybu. I think you can guess why you are here. Abdul. His voice was deep or maybe it was just the helmet. Abdul replied meekly. N-no sir? 

Ahsan stepped forward and leaned close enough to be face to helmet with Abdul. I am disappointed you try to hide your guilt. He stepped away. What have you told the Sybuic state to our east, Abdul? Abdul's heart began to race. I-what? You accuse me of this? I would n-never! I love the Sealiphat- 

[b]*T H O C K*[/b]

The side of Abdul's face was hit by Ahsan's staff, Keep my beloved state's name out of your traitorous mouth. Now you will die either way, the only difference is whether or not it is swift. He pointed the pointy star at the end of his staff at Abdul Now. What did you tell them? 

Abdul spat at Ahsan saliva mixed with blood landed upon his robe. I told them where to find your mother- Another smack was laid upon Abduls' cheek. Hasan, I thank you for putting aside our differences and fetching this practical apostate for me. Bring me his head when youre done. Ahsan turned and left, closing the door behind him as Hasan stood up and produced his implements[/i]
[/spoiler]
